1.d4 Nf6 2.Nf3 d5 3.e3 e6 4.Bd3 Bd6 5.O-.strategy: Prepares to develop the queen's bishop on the long diagonal, where it supports the central break instead of sitting behind the e3 pawn. A patient, flexible plan: the b-pawn also backs a later c4. The bishop stays behind its own d4 pawn until the centre opens.

Develops the queenside knight so that it supports a central pawn break, keeping the c-pawn free. The cost is that the knight shuts in the light-squared bishop, which has to find another route out, so Black's development stays a little passive.
